model_conventions.checked_scope: Every definition and theorem is compared after expanding score inequalities to ordinal comparisons. No result uses addition, distance, or cardinal significance of preference scores.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: Each source strict preference ordering is represented by an injective real-valued score. Only comparisons of scores carry preference meaning; their magnitudes do not.
model_conventions.why_needed: The source uses abstract complete transitive strict relations, while the reusable assignment and deferred-acceptance library consumes real-valued comparison functions. Injectivity is exactly the no-ties condition on a finite carrier.

model_conventions.checked_scope: All source-facing marriage theorems require the complete strict domain for true and reported profiles. Positivity is not treated as a separate economic assumption, and dummy padding used for the general finite case also stays positive.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: Positive scores place every opposite-side participant above the reusable library's zero-valued unmatched option. This encodes the source marriage model's complete feasible partner lists and its requirement that a marriage outcome leave nobody unmatched.
model_conventions.why_needed: The reusable assignment carrier permits partial assignments and uses zero when an agent is unmatched, whereas the source marriage model uses an invertible complete match and complete strict rankings over the entire opposite side.

model_conventions.checked_scope: Every named theorem is audited at its finite source instantiation. Stability bridges prove completeness on equal positive strict markets; efficiency and incentive quantifiers range only over legal reports; no conclusion is inferred from the polymorphic type or a selector name.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: The reusable Assignment type is a mutually consistent partial one-to-one carrier and the score-table aliases are polymorphic. The source marriage interpretation is obtained only after imposing finite equal sides, legal strict profiles, and the complete-outcome or source-stability endpoint.
model_conventions.why_needed: Roth defines a finite balanced marriage problem with invertible outcomes, while reusable library types also support unmatched agents, unequal sides, and generic carriers. The broader carrier is representation infrastructure and cannot by itself receive source credit.

model_conventions.checked_scope: Nonemptiness is visible in the affected PaperInterface theorem binders. It supplies only an inhabited source market and no matching, stability, incentive, or Pareto conclusion.
model_conventions.formal_meaning: Named-agent and first-choice results are instantiated on nonempty participant sides. Equal cardinality then supplies nonemptiness of the opposite side where needed.

model_conventions.why_needed: Corollary 5.1 selects a true first choice, and Theorem 6's assertion that no outcome is strictly preferred by all men would have a vacuous universal comparison in an empty market. The source presents agents and first choices rather than an empty-market edge case.
